title: DNS Resolution Failure Troubleshooting
summary: Diagnose and resolve common Domain Name System (DNS) failures in Cisco Packet Tracer, including misconfigured client DNS server addresses, disabled DNS daemon services, and missing A/CNAME resource records, verifying systematic remediation using ipconfig, nslookup, ping, and web browsers.
learning_objectives: Isolate DNS resolution issues from underlying layer 1 through layer 3 IP network transport failures
Verify and correct client DNS resolver settings using ipconfig and IP configuration interfaces
Diagnose DNS server service status and activate disabled DNS daemon processes on server endpoints
Identify and create missing Address (A) and Canonical Name (CNAME) resource records in the authoritative DNS database
Utilize nslookup to query specific DNS servers, distinguish server timeouts from non-existent domain errors, and inspect resource records
Validate end-to-end name resolution and HTTP web portal delivery following systematic remediation

source.origin: Independently authored network services troubleshooting laboratory guide based on IETF RFC 1034, RFC 1035, and RFC 7230 standards
